noInherit.description: If true, the annotation is not inherited by mixins.

stayInEngine.description:
An annotation indicating whether this function should be executed in the same engine from which it was called
if possible. For languages besides Java, the default is `true` for client-side engines and `false` for server-side
for performance reasons (i.e. executing in Java server-side will usually be more performant), though for functions
that take or return `native` values, the implementing SDK may choose to stay in engine by default server-side.

The value of the `stayInEngine` is either a boolean or a map of {@link Action.Requirements}s to booleans.
To set the value `true` for **all** engines (besides js-server), simply set the value of the annotation to `true`.
To set the value for all engines for a given language,
use {@link ImplLanguage#dslName} as the key.

In the following example,
    * `needsToStayInEngine` will always stay in its engine (except for js-server)
    * `needsToStayInPy` will always stay in a Python engine, but will use the Java implementation when called
       from server-side JavaScript
    * `needsToStayInPyFoo` will only override the default behavior for engines which {@link Action.Engine#canRun}
       `py-foo` requirement
```type
@call(stayInEngine=true)
needsToStayInEngine: function() java | js | py

@call(stayInEngine={'py': true})
needsToStayInPy: function() java | js | py

@call(stayInEngine={'py-foo': true})
needsToStayInPyFoo: function() java | js | py
```

@see MethodType#inline

javaThreadAffinity.description:
If true then this method or all methods in a given type will only get executes in the same Java Thread in a given
C3 Server node

nodeRole.description:
An expression that can calculate target server role or possible roles where this action should execute.

Scope for the expression is arguments of the C3 action call. I.e. expression can refer to args of the action. E.g.
`@call(node='[ "task", "leader" ]')` on `Cron.c3typ` ensures that cron job will run on one of the `task` node
but if none available then will run on one of the `leader` node. Note that `this` is an implicit argument to all
member functions.

Result of the expression can be an array OR a single string value.  E.g. `Dataset.c3typ` can have
`@call(nodeRole='"data"')` in which case only data nodes will be used for stateful datasets and if there is no
node pool with role `data` then corresponding action will fail.

Also note that this annotation can be declared on a function or on a type; however if it is declared on the type
then it will only apply to methods explicitly declared on that type.

If this annotation is declared on the type then expression scope needs to be valid for both static and member
methods; i.e. `this` can be either parent type or instance depending if method is static or member respectively.

@see #app
@see #nodePool
@see #node
@see #threadPool

nodePool.description:
An expression that can calculate target server node pool where this action should execute.

Scope for the expression is arguments of the C3 action call. I.e. expression can refer to args of the action. E.g.
`@call(node='this.nodePool()')` on `Job.c3typ` ensures that actions are dispatched to specific node pool where
we expect this job to run. Note that `this` is an implicit argument to all member functions.

Result of the expression can be an array OR a single string value. E.g. `MyMlTrainingJob.c3typ` can have
`@call(nodePool='[ "ml-train", "task" ]')` so that instances of such jobs can run on node-pool named `ml-train`,
but if there is no such node-pool then will fall back to default `task` node-pool.

Also note that this annotation can be declared on a function or on a type; however if it is declared on the type
then it will only apply to methods explicitly declared on that type.

If this annotation is declared on the type then expression scope needs to be valid for both static and member
methods; i.e. `this` can be either parent type or instance depending if method is static or member respectively.

@see #app
@see #nodeRole
@see #node
@see #threadPool

dispatcher.description:
If `true` then this method is considered as part of a dispatching logic so has special semantics, e.g. not having
it's own context such as authz, client version, etc

declaredTypeOnly.description:
If true then this static method can only be invoked from the type it is declared on. This annotation can only be
used on static methods and such methods can not be overridden.

title:
Special annotations for methods (functions).

Three modifiers of a method declaration are exclusive.
 - `abstract` means types that mixin this type are assumed to implement it
 - `optional` means types that mixin this type only implement it if they declare it
 - `final` means types that mixin this type may not override it

The difference between abstract and final is that abstract indicates that an implementation is necessary, but not
supplied by the originally declaring type. Any type that mixes in the type is presumed to implement all abstract
methods (unless it re-declares them as abstract). Optional methods are also not implemented by the originally
declaring type, but they represent optional operations that need not be implemented by child types that mixin
if not appropriate. If a type intends to implement an optional method, it must declare it.

In the case of both abstract and optional, if the method is called but not implemented on the type it is being
called on, an error occurs.
name: Ann.Call
